Glory be to the name of Jesus. I thank my Mother a million times for making me a witness to her apparition on this holy land.
My name is Sona Jaison. I am a member of Vettukad Parish in the Thrissur Diocese. This is my daughter Jasvia, this is my son Joshua, and this is my husband’s mother.
I first took the Covenant on 20-11-23. Let me share the circumstances behind it. On August 12, my husband passed away.
After that, I was in a state of depression. Two months before his death, my son was diagnosed with a condition called “Fits.”
The doctor told both of us that there is a chance he might develop autism, that his growth could slow down, and his speech and other abilities might regress.
Sometimes he would walk with unsteady steps. Even after turning one year old, he could not walk properly. It was when he was one year and one month old that this illness was confirmed.

At that time, I was very afraid. I was already in deep depression then. We had shown him to the doctor and started his medication.
It was during that period that my husband’s death happened. He was attacked due to dengue fever.
Even after the fever subsided, due to a difference in blood circulation, a clot formed, which led to the attack.
It happened completely unexpectedly. To tell the truth, it shook me to the core.
As Father says, my whole world collapsed. I didn’t know how to move forward or how to live anymore.
I used to do a small tailoring job, but I had no fixed income. The doctor had specifically said that my son needed special care until the age of five.
I didn’t know what to do. When my husband died, we had small loans taken here and there — like those from women’s self-help groups — totaling around three to three and a half lakh rupees.
Every month, I had to pay about ten thousand rupees in installments. While he was alive, we somehow managed to pay that amount, bit by bit.
After his death, I was terrified — how would I repay the money? I thought maybe I could work and pay it off, but I couldn’t go for work.
There was no one I could leave my son with; I had to take care of him until he turned five. Fear completely overwhelmed me.
I was so scared that I decided to end my life. But I couldn’t bring myself to harm my children.
I had asked them from Jesus — I had prayed specifically for my first child to be a daughter, and He gave her to me; then I prayed for a son, and He blessed me with him.
At that point, I couldn’t bring myself to harm them with my own hands. But I wanted to die — I just wanted somehow to go to my husband, to see him again.
Those were the thoughts running through my mind. While thinking about suicide, I began to wonder how I could die peacefully.
I thought, if I want to die without pain, what should I do? Then an idea came to me —
I could take sleeping pills, give them to my children too, make sure they were gone, and then I could die.
But I knew sleeping pills were not easily available like that.
So, from the third day after my husband’s death, I started telling everyone that I wanted to see a psychiatrist — that I wasn’t able to cope anymore.
My poor mother believed me and took me to several places.
First, we met a priest in our area who was also a psychiatrist.
Through that priest, I was referred to a psychiatrist named Dr. Jomey at Jubilee Mission Hospital.
The doctor spoke with me and said he would prescribe some medicines. He asked how my sleep was.
When I was about to say that I couldn’t sleep, my mother interrupted and said, “She has no trouble sleeping, Doctor.”
Then the doctor said, “In that case, we don’t need to prescribe sleeping pills.” I felt disappointed.
So the doctor said, “Let’s do one thing — I’ll prescribe some medicines to help your mind relax.” He gave the prescription.
To be honest, even my mother didn’t know my true intention. The poor woman took so much trouble for me, taking me from place to place.
After some time, the doctor called my mother personally and said, “Try to keep her in a different environment for a while — maybe stay with you. That will help.”  My mother agreed to it.
Then my mother took me home. I stayed there for a month, taking the medicines, and I began to feel better. After
that, I went back to the hospital to see the doctor, and on the 41st day after my husband’s death, I returned home.
By then, I felt my mind had become stable. I thought, maybe I could stop the medicines now. But while talking to the doctor, I told him,
“Doctor, I’m not sleeping well at night. I still wake up to feed my son milk.”
I said, “I’m staying at my husband’s house now. Could you please change the medicine a little?”
The doctor replied, “Alright then, let’s stop the sleeping pills.”
To be honest, I hadn’t even realized there were sleeping pills in my prescription. But by then my mind had improved; I thought I could manage everything now.
My mind was relaxed, and I returned home after the 41st day rituals. Everyone who had come for the prayers left, and finally my mother said goodbye and went home.
I was left alone in that house. I had never stayed even a single day without my husband or my mother.
We had lived together for only six years. We were married in 2017.
I began to hate God deeply. To tell the truth, I don’t think there’s anyone else who has hated God as much as I did.
I asked Him, “I prepared myself so much before entering this marriage. I wasn’t even interested in marriage, but I prayed and sought Your will.”
“It was You who gave him to me — so why did You take him away?” I asked.
I said, “My God must truly be heartless, just as everyone says — a God without compassion.”
I even began to hate my Mother Mary. I told her, “You also stood with them, didn’t you? You didn’t say a single word for me, not even for the sake of your son’s child.”
“You joined with them too, didn’t you?” I said. Because after marriage, my husband and I had only one special trip together — to Puthenpally Church in Thrissur.
Every Friday, we used to go there for the novena. So I asked the Blessed Mother, “Mother, why did You abandon me too?”
My husband was the unit president in the parish and was very close to the church. So then I even began to hate St. Joseph.
I said to him, “Why did You also forsake me? My husband was just like You — a hardworking and righteous man. Why did You let this happen?”
“None of You had any mercy on me!” I said. I hated them — truly hated them — with all my heart.
Slowly, the depression came back again. I searched for the prescription and found it. That week, things were terrible — I fell sick with a fever, and my son too.
My daughter had fever, I had fever, my son had fever. My daughter was crying; I couldn’t carry her. My body was so weak — I have a uric acid problem, and back then it was severe.
I don’t even know if anyone can understand — even the space between my little fingers hurt. I couldn’t lift my son at all. Everything was too much.
While I was in that depressed state, a woman — a sister I didn’t even know — came to see me. I don’t know if I had ever met her before in our parish.
My mother had spoken to her at the church, sharing her worries about me. That’s how this sister —
a complete stranger — came to visit me. She sat beside me as I held the prescription below my pillow.
That sister came to my house, took some blessed oil, and anointed my forehead. She sprinkled salt around my room and said, “I will show you the place where you can find deliverance”
I had heard about Kreupasanam before, back when my husband was alive. I even had a leaflet from there at home, which I wrapped clothes to pack and gave them after tailoring.
But honestly, I didn’t know much about it. Still, I trusted that sister completely, even though I didn’t understand everything. When you are close to death, even a little spark of hope feels precious.
At the insistence of my mother-in-law and that sister, I was finally taken there — it was just a delay of one or two days.
I came here and took the Covenant. For a long time, I hadn’t been able to sleep properly, but that day I slept peacefully.
To tell the truth, I didn’t even hear the first part of the class properly because I was sleeping so soundly.
During the session, when the counselor spoke about praying for each illness, and when epilepsy was mentioned, I suddenly sat upright.
The words from the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 17, verses 14 to 21 — about Jesus healing the boy with epilepsy — deeply touched my heart.
I wrote that verse down. I also wrote about my daughter’s speech delay, for which I had found another verse.
But that particular verse about the epileptic boy strongly moved me — it felt as if someone was telling me directly, “I will heal your son’s illness. You must believe firmly in this Word.”
From that day until today, I have never missed that prayer during our family prayer time. Even my daughter knows that verse by heart.
When we recite that verse in church, my daughter turns to look at me and smiles — because she knows I have never once stopped praying it.
After coming here and taking the Covenant, I went back home. Among the six intentions I placed in the Covenant, the first one was this — I wanted to have my own source of income.
To be honest, I’ve always been a person with a bit of self-respect and pride. Since childhood, I’ve never liked troubling anyone — not even for a small thing like a candy.
My parents or my husband would give me what I needed, and I’d accept it, but I never used to ask or trouble anyone for my needs.
Even with my husband, I never used to burden him with my personal requests. So the first thing I told Mother Mary in my Covenant was,
“I need a source of income — a steady income — and You must give it to me, because this is about my survival.”
“If I have to bow my head in shame before others because my husband is gone, then my life is over. I don’t want to live a life of humiliation.”
Since childhood, I’ve cried through many phases. When I was a teenager, people used to say, “Once you start working, everything will be fine.”
After I started working, they said, “Once you get married, you’ll find happiness.” I believed that, and I got married. Though my husband and I had our small disagreements like anyone else,
he was the one who truly showed me the light of day — he gave me a reason to live.
That’s why his loss was so painful. During my working days, I used to leave home at 9:00 a.m. and return around 6:30 p.m.
I hardly ever saw daylight at home. Even on Sundays, I was busy with studies — plus one, plus two, then degree classes —
so I never really knew what a Sunday felt like. That’s why the first request I made to the Blessed Mother was for a stable income.
Secondly, I asked the Mother to heal my son’s illness — because I didn’t want to see my son as an autistic child or as one who would not grow properly.
I told her, “Mother, this child is a gift I asked from you — so I want him to be completely healthy.”
“If he remains in that condition when he grows up, I won’t be able to carry on; I will collapse.”
So I prayed, “Please make him stable and whole.” That was my second covenant intention.
The third covenant intention was my husband’s greatest dream — to build a house. That was his desire, and I placed that as part of my covenant too before returning home.
Then, to my amazement, my son slowly began to recover. He started walking, speaking, and became very active.
Even I was astonished. When I took him to the doctor, the doctor said there was a remarkable improvement and advised to stop the medication.
Actually, it wasn’t the doctor who stopped the medicine — I did. I told the doctor, “My son is healed; he no longer needs these medicines.”
The doctor had earlier said that he would need to continue medication until the age of five. But I told the doctor, “No,
I still have the last prescription the doctor gave to continue the medicines." I stopped them myself.
The doctor said, “If he ever gets a fever, make sure to give this medicine again — he must not have another seizure. For now, he’s fine; we can let him be.”
All this happened during the time my husband had passed away.
Even then, the doctor told me, “He’s doing well now.” But I said, “No, doctor — my Mother touched and healed him.”
Earlier, I had already come here. Despite my heavy schedule and exhaustion, I came here and showed my son’s condition to the Mother.
When I met Father Joseph and he placed his hand on my son’s head, the peace I experienced that day — I cannot describe it.
When Father touched and blessed him, he gently tapped my son’s cheek and smiled — he didn’t say a single word, just smiled. I didn’t really understand the meaning of that smile at the time.
I wondered, “Why didn’t Father say anything?” Then he gave me a blessed medal. As I was leaving that day,
the sister who was with me said, “Don’t keep that in your hand — you must hang it around your son’s neck.”
From that very day, his illness disappeared. From then until the medal fell from his neck into my hand, I never removed it once.
I had placed it on him that day, and from that moment, I began to notice great changes in him.
Today, he’s even more active than my daughter.
The joy I feel whenever I cry — when he comes to wipe off my tears— it’s beyond words.
I didn’t understand then why Father remained silent that day, but later, during the Covenant worship, I realized it.
I’m someone who never misses the Covenant worship. Even my daughter scolds me sometimes because, when I’m at work, I keep listening to it.
Earlier, I used to listen to songs; now, I only listen to worship. Since 2017, I’ve been listening regularly — if I don’t hear the worship, my tailoring doesn’t feel right.
One day, while listening, Father said, “Those who don’t receive an answer immediately are the ones who will receive the greatest blessings.”
That’s when I understood why Father didn’t say anything when he blessed my son.
I fully believed that my son was completely healed, and from that day onward, I never even opened that medicine packet again.
Since then, he has had fever and several minor illnesses, but I never gave him that medicine again — not even once.
That medicine is still kept in my bag — only so that I can show it as proof when I give this
testimony. Otherwise, I would have thrown it away that very day. From that day till now, he has never fallen sick again.
For that, I owe countless thanks to Jesus and to Mother Mary, because if he hadn’t recovered, I too would have slowly fallen into depression and would never have been able to move forward with my life.
Gradually, my daughter’s speech delay also began to improve. Earlier, she couldn’t pronounce words properly; even when she tried to talk, her speech wasn’t clear.
But I would always anoint her tongue and forehead with holy oil and give her blessed salt. She loved the honey—she would happily take it.
Slowly, she began to speak more clearly.
Then she had another problem — a severe allergy with a terrible cough. Whenever that cough started, she would cry at night, crying and gasping for breath.
The problem was that my son too needed attention, but it was her father who used to take her when she cried.
After his death, since he wasn’t there anymore, I had to comfort her myself. I tried my best not to let her cry.
One night, when I was wondering what to do, I suddenly remembered the blessed medal.
I took it and placed it around her neck. From that very day, her cough disappeared — completely healed.
Later, when I was thinking about what to do for my livelihood, I was praying for clarity. During one of the reflections at the church, I heard about “Mother Mary’s work — tailoring.”
To be honest, I had no interest in tailoring. After my husband’s death, I had gone into deep depression; I was even afraid to buy fabric, cut it, or stitch anything. I was scared of it.
But then I thought, “Isn’t this Mother Mary’s own work?”
That too happened a month before my husband passed away. I was sorting through the cabin at that time, and I realized that God had kept it for me.
I started working on it, and things began moving forward. It became a good source of income for me.
Gradually, I even started receiving orders from Canada. Twice, I stitched dresses and sent them there, which earned me some income.
One of those dresses was for a dance competition. It was joy because they informed me that they won first place at the state-level dance competition in Canada. I was immensely happy.
After that, I received another order, stitched it, and continued my sewing work. Eventually, I even hired a staff member to help with the work.
In the meantime, I was still worried about paying off debts and thinking about what to do when I got a call from LIC.
They offered me a part-time job, and I thought, “Yes, this is the work I can do while keeping my children in mind.”
I took that job, and I started earning commission from it. With the sewing and the commission work combined, I managed to handle all my responsibilities.
Until today, I remember the first time I told Mother Mary that I wanted to be able to give my daughter anything she asked for — even a small sweet. I promised that I would provide for her.
I’m not someone who gives everything in exact order or sequence, but I’ve been able to provide for everything she truly needed and stay by her side.
With that, her needs have been taken care of. Even when small family problems arose, they never became unmanageable, because I was able to handle things steadily.
Nothing happened immediately. But I thought, “If something happens to me, my children must have something secured.” That was something my husband had wished for, so I thought I should start building a house.
At the time I decided to start the house, grandfather passed away. Then I thought, “Now, grandfather isn’t here…” I fell into depression.
Even while feeling that way, Brother said it’s okay, there’s no problem. “You can start; we can do it together,” he said.
So I began the house work. By the third month, I didn’t even know how much money I had — I had nothing. I had no idea how I would manage this construction.
I had a little gold, but how could that possibly cover the work of a house? I didn’t know if it was my desire or God’s will. To understand, I went to Father for guidance.
Even then, Father placed that document to Mother and didn’t say anything; but I understood that silence meant it was good. I trusted it. I told my mother everything: “Mother, I’m going to
start. I don’t even know the price of a brick, a bag of cement, or a rod. I don’t know the square foot of a house, but I will begin.”
Despite knowing nothing, I started the house work. I didn’t know who would supply what, or how the work would
be contracted. People told me how it would be managed and assured me that everything would be taken care of.
I relied on their guidance, and even without money in hand, I got the contractors to start the work. Within six months, the house construction was completed.
This coming 18th, I will move into my new house. I came to invite my mother, the one who helped rebuild my collapsed home, the one who was my support.
I can honestly say that. I have completed the intentions I submitted, and I feel that I no longer need to put any.
But when I renewed the first covenant intention I had made with Mother last time, I said — I want to remain in Your covenant until my death.
I have no requests, but I want to stay in Your covenant until I die — because there is a truth that only I, God, and Mother know.
Deep inside me lies a kind of depression — like waves resting before a tsunami, or a mountain quietly waiting before a landslide. Hidden within are many silent depressions.
I have no future ahead. I have no partner. I have to carry this burden all my life.
I constantly worry about how I will raise my children — that fear and depression lies at one end.
That’s when I told Jesus everything. I got the word. And I opened the book of Isaiah 45.
“Your Maker is your Husband; the Lord of hosts is His name.”
From that moment, I gave my husband’s place to my Jesus. The role of a father in our home is also fulfilled by my Jesus. From then on, I never had to look back.
Everything in my life has since happened in ways that astonish me.
As part of my apostolic work, I buy newspapers and distribute them house to house. I tell my story as I give them.
My daughter sometimes asks, “Mom, why are you giving these?” And I tell her, “If your mother stands alive before you today, it’s because of this paper.”
I tell her that, and so I keep distributing newspapers. After that, I began to do acts of mercy, as I had promised. Even though I live in poverty,
not even my household knows — sometimes I get 300 rupees from tailoring, I will give 100 to others. This is something I have told Mother Mary about.
I have given to many people quietly; no one else knows. Near our house, the husband of a woman had an accident — nobody knew — so I
went to the hospital to see her and personally gave her 2,000 rupees. I said this because
The very next day, someone came and returned 4,000 rupees to me. That’s when I realized that God returns to us fourfold. From
that moment, I began to give joyfully. Since my youth, I have given, but now I give as if it’s credited to my Jesus.
I always tell people, “Mother told me to give.” If anyone asks who told me, I speak of Mother and say, “If you can, please go to the place.”
Regarding the change that came to me, to be honest, I saw the Mass outside, I received my children from God but
I saw the Mass outside. After taking the Covenant here, gradually things began to change.
I began to go inside the church, and then I started looking at Father (the priest) and attending Holy Mass. As I prayed, I fixed my eyes on the Crucified image on the altar.
One day, when the construction of our church altar was completed and they opened it for public viewing, I saw a vision that words cannot fully describe. I don’t know if anyone else in the parish noticed it.
Above the Crucified image, there was a photo of God the Father, with His two hands stretched out. The moment I saw it, I felt
as if someone whispered in my ear, saying: “If I was willing to sacrifice My Son for you, how precious must you be to Me?”
That moment gave me strength and courage. Truly speaking, when I came out from there, my bank account was at zero balance. Living alone
with my children as a family, with all the usual expenses — electricity bills, cable bills, and such — I still had no fear.
Because even when I look back today, I can only marvel at how God has sustained me all along. The God
who has carried me this far will continue to carry me until my death — that is the faith that strengthens me.
After my husband’s death, when I came here and took the Covenant, I began wearing the covenant medal on my chest. Since then, I have been noticing something remarkable.
Sometimes I place my hand on my chest to feel my heartbeat — but I cannot even feel it beating. It feels as though someone has kept it safely within their hands.
Earlier, during exams, my heart used to beat fast — it’s indescribable. But now, no matter what troubles come my way, when I place my
hand on my heart, I truly feel as though it’s resting peacefully there, as if a little child’s heart is being held gently in someone’s palm.
I didn’t even realize it — you know the kind of tension people usually have when building a house? I had none. Everyone was surprised.
When I called and said, “On the 18th, my housewarming” everyone asked, “Didn’t you just say you were about to start the construction? You’re now saying it’s finished already?”
When I told them the house was completed within six months, everyone was astonished. Even the workers who came to demolish
the old structure told me, “Sister, you’re truly blessed. Many have started building homes long before you and still haven’t finished theirs.”
They said, “There’s surely a special grace upon you.”
And during that time, there were heavy rains — the day they declared a red alert was the same day the main roofing work of
my house was going on. But not a single drop of rain fell until the roof was completed. Only after that did it rain heavily.
Everyone said, “Sister, this is truly a miracle.”
I told them, “When the foundation was laid, I had established a blessed medal from Father. I placed it under the  foundation before construction began.”
I said, “This is not a house that I am building — this is a house built by my
Mother Mary and my Jesus together. I don’t need to be anxious; They will do it the way They will.”
When the final stage came and the money started running out, I began to feel anxious. But then I sat quietly for a while, and the Holy Spirit spoke within me:
“Did you truly trusted not in God, or in the money that was in your hands?”
That moment made me realize the truth. When I let go of my anxiety, everything began to move smoothly again.
On the coming 18th, we will have the house blessing ceremony.
It amazes me — it’s truly wondrous. From the moment I thought my life was broken and I had no future ahead, Jesus held my hand and began walking with me.
No storm or sunshine has been able to harm me since — because I have a God who sustains me through everything.
For that, I offer countless thanks to my Jesus and to my Mother Mary, who my Jesus gave me. I conclude my testimony here.
St. Mark, in the Gospel of Mark, chapter 12, verse 43, says: He called His disciples near and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more into the treasury than all others.”
Father Joseph always reminded us of this — how much spiritual wealth we have matters more than material wealth. He reminded us to consider the spiritual deposits we make.
When you give from what you have, what is its true value? This is something we must constantly reflect upon — a great lesson on covenant.
Life itself is a strong testimony of God’s manifestation. God’s experience with the Israelites is a parallel — as Sona describes it here, our covenant life is made powerful through active faith.
Life is now very strong. Even after my husband passed away in August, within a year, my daughter experienced such a great recovery.
Today, I can say everything is fulfilled. I can bring my daughter to the altar and testify — Jesus has completely filled her life.
As Paul say, Christ must be formed in me; I am experiencing this for your sake.
Let us pray for Christ to be formed in us. Let us offer this testimony, blessed by Jesus and the Blessed Mother, in honor of the great witness of the Sona.
